sample_unit: responses (55 questions x 6 chatbots, first round)

links.outcome: Reproducibility of safety classifications across two rounds of identical prompts
links.effect: Safety classifications agreed in 97.3% of pairs (κ=0.821); 9 safety classifications changed across rounds (5 safe to unsafe, 4 unsafe to safe).
links.quote: Nine safety classifications changed across the 2 rounds (5 from safe to unsafe and 4 from unsafe to safe).

links.outcome: Unsafe responses to COPD questions by public-facing LLM chatbots
links.effect: Unsafe responses occurred in every model: 4 (7.3%) each for ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot, DeepSeek; 5 (9.1%) Qwen; 6 (10.9%) Doubao.
links.quote: Unsafe responses occurred in every model: ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot, and DeepSeek each generated 4 unsafe responses (7.3%); Qwen generated 5 (9.1%); and Doubao generated 6 (10.9%).

links.outcome: Readability of LLM-generated COPD health advice
links.effect: Readability indices differed significantly across models; specific grade levels are not reported in the abstract.
links.quote: Accuracy, empathy, information-quality measures, source-transparency scores, and readability indices differed significantly across models.

screen.reason: The study evaluates and compares the performance, safety, and stability of 6 commercial LLM chatbots in answering COPD-related consumer health questions using a standardized 55-question benchmark.
